mainEntity.name: Why does alcohol have more calories than carbs or protein?

acceptedAnswer.text: Alcohol provides about 7 calories per gram, compared with 4 calories per gram for carbohydrates and protein — a big part of why drinks add up faster than their serving size might suggest.

mainEntity.name: Are cocktails always higher in calories than beer or wine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, but not always — it depends on the recipe. Cocktails with sugary mixers, syrups or cream can be far higher in calories than a spirit with soda water or a glass of dry wine.

In the United States, one standard drink contains about 14 grams (0.6 fl oz) of pure alcohol — roughly a 12-oz beer at 5%, a 5-oz glass of wine at 12%, or a 1.5-oz shot of 40% spirits. A UK unit is smaller, at 8 grams.

mainEntity.name: Does the calculator include the calories from mixers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you enter them. Choose Custom and add the carbs per drink, or use the spirit-and-soda preset, which adds 20 g of sugar (80 kcal) to the alcohol calories.

mainEntity.name: How many calories are in a standard drink?

acceptedAnswer.text: A US standard drink holds 14 g of pure alcohol, which is about 98 kcal from the alcohol alone. Carbs in beer, wine or mixers come on top.

mainEntity.name: Does light beer really save calories?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. With this calculator's presets, a light 4.2% beer is about 106 kcal against 150 kcal for a regular 5% beer, a saving of about 44 kcal per drink.

mainEntity.name: Which alcoholic drink has the fewest calories?

acceptedAnswer.text: Per standard drink the alcohol calories are about the same, roughly 98 kcal. Straight spirits and hard seltzer have the fewest carbs, so they come out lowest, but drinking more of them erases the saving.

mainEntity.name: Why do my results differ from a drink label?

acceptedAnswer.text: Labels include the actual carbs and sugar of the brand, which vary widely. Enter the carbs from the label under Custom for a closer figure.
